title.en: Micturition and the composition of urine

body.en: Urine formed by the nephrons is carried to the urinary bladder and stored until a voluntary signal is given by the central nervous system. Stretch receptors in the bladder wall send signals to the CNS as it fills; the CNS sends motor messages that contract the smooth muscles of the bladder and relax the urethral sphincter, releasing urine. This process is *micturition*, and the neural mechanism causing it is the micturition reflex. An adult excretes on average 1 to 1.5 litres of urine a day. Urine is a light yellow watery fluid, slightly acidic (pH 6.0), with a characteristic odour; on average 25–30 g of urea is excreted per day. Glucose (glycosuria) and ketone bodies (ketonuria) in urine indicate diabetes mellitus.
body.kn: ಮೂತ್ರಕೋಶ ತುಂಬಿದಾಗ ಹಿಗ್ಗುವ ಗ್ರಾಹಕಗಳು ಕೇಂದ್ರ ನರವ್ಯೂಹಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಕೇತ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ಮೂತ್ರಕೋಶದ ಸ್ನಾಯುಗಳು ಸಂಕೋಚಿಸಿ ಮೂತ್ರ ಹೊರಬರುತ್ತದೆ — ಇದೇ ಮೂತ್ರ ವಿಸರ್ಜನೆ. ವಯಸ್ಕರು ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ 1–1.5 ಲೀಟರ್ ಮೂತ್ರ ವಿಸರ್ಜಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ; pH ಸುಮಾರು 6.0; ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ 25–30 ಗ್ರಾಂ ಯೂರಿಯಾ.

say.en: As the bladder fills, stretch receptors signal the CNS. The CNS makes the bladder muscle contract and the urethral sphincter relax.
Normal urine: 1 to 1.5 litres a day, slightly acidic, with 25 to 30 grams of urea. Glucose or ketones in urine point to diabetes mellitus.
If the kidneys fail, urea builds up: uremia. Haemodialysis cleans the blood outside the body.

right.en: Remove about 200 mL of CO2 a minute
Puts bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol and broken-down drugs into bile

Urea builds up in the blood; treated by haemodialysis

explanation.en: Kidneys do most of the work, but lungs, liver and skin also remove wastes. When the kidneys fail, an artificial kidney (dialysis) or a kidney transplant can save a life.

say.en: Match the other organs that remove wastes and the common kidney disorders.

body.en: Lungs remove large amounts of CO2 (about 200 mL per minute) and significant amounts of water every day. The liver, the largest gland, secretes bile containing bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins and drugs, which mostly pass out with digestive wastes. Sweat from sweat glands is a watery fluid with NaCl, small amounts of urea and lactic acid; its main job is cooling the body. Sebaceous glands remove sterols, hydrocarbons and waxes through sebum. Small amounts of nitrogenous wastes are also removed in saliva.
body.kn: ಶ್ವಾಸಕೋಶಗಳು ನಿಮಿಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಮಾರು 200 ಮಿ.ಲೀ CO2 ಹೊರಹಾಕುತ್ತವೆ. ಯಕೃತ್ತಿನ ಪಿತ್ತರಸದಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಲಿರುಬಿನ್, ಬಿಲಿವರ್ಡಿನ್, ಕೊಲೆಸ್ಟರಾಲ್ ಇರುತ್ತವೆ. ಬೆವರಿನಲ್ಲಿ NaCl, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಯೂರಿಯಾ ಮತ್ತು ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲ; ಮೇದೋಗ್ರಂಥಿಗಳು ಸ್ಟೀರಾಲ್, ಹೈಡ್ರೋಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮೇಣ ಹೊರಹಾಕುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Liver: bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, drugs in bile
Sweat: NaCl, little urea, lactic acid

body.en: Malfunction of the kidneys can cause accumulation of urea in blood, a condition called uremia, which is highly harmful and may lead to kidney failure. Urea can be removed by haemodialysis: blood is drawn from a convenient artery, mixed with an anticoagulant such as heparin, and pumped through a dialysing unit where a cellophane tube is bathed in dialysing fluid that has the same composition as plasma except the nitrogenous wastes. Nitrogenous wastes move out by diffusion; the cleared blood is pumped back through a vein after adding anti-heparin. Kidney transplantation is the ultimate method for acute renal failure, ideally from a close relative to reduce rejection. Renal calculi are stones or insoluble masses of crystallised salts (oxalates etc.) in the kidney. Glomerulonephritis is inflammation of the glomeruli of the kidney.
body.kn: ರಕ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ಯೂರಿಯಾ ಶೇಖರಣೆಯೇ ಯೂರೀಮಿಯಾ. ಹಿಮೋಡಯಾಲಿಸಿಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಪರಿನ್ ಸೇರಿಸಿದ ರಕ್ತವನ್ನು ಡಯಾಲಿಸಿಂಗ್ ದ್ರವದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಸೆಲ್ಲೋಫೇನ್ ನಳಿಕೆಯ ಮೂಲಕ ಹಾಯಿಸಿ ತ್ಯಾಜ್ಯವನ್ನು ವಿಸರಣದಿಂದ ತೆಗೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಮೂತ್ರಪಿಂಡದ ಕಲ್ಲುಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಗ್ಲಾಮೆರುಲೋನೆಫ್ರೈಟಿಸ್ ಇತರ ಅಸ್ವಸ್ಥತೆಗಳು.

points.en: Uremia: urea builds up in blood
Dialysing fluid = plasma minus nitrogenous wastes
Renal calculi: crystallised salts; glomerulonephritis: inflamed glomeruli

problem.en: In a dialysis machine, why does urea leave the blood but glucose and sodium do not, even though both are small enough to cross the cellophane membrane?

steps.en: Substances cross the cellophane membrane by diffusion, from higher to lower concentration.
The dialysing fluid has the same composition as plasma except that it has no nitrogenous wastes.
So there is a concentration gradient only for urea and other nitrogenous wastes; glucose and Na+ are at the same concentration on both sides and show no net movement.

answer.en: Only nitrogenous wastes have a concentration gradient, because the dialysing fluid matches plasma in everything else
